title: CHAPTER 12: QUICK REVISION :KEY FACTS, DATES AND MNEMONICS

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Includes key historical dates in the context of Hindi and Rajbhasha.
Provides quick reference guides for constitutional articles related to official language provisions.
Summarizes prominent awards related to Hindi language and literature.
Features a quick revision guide for Hindi grammar and memory-boosting mnemonics for competitive exams.
Offers an exam-specific checklist tailored for the Rajbhasha Adhikari examination.

cells: Constitution of India came into force; Hindi declared Official Language under Article 343
Constituent Assembly adopted Hindi as Official Language; observed as Hindi Diwas every year
Date by which Hindi was to completely replace English (as per Art. 343(2)); not implemented; Official Languages Act 1963 extended English's use
First World Hindi Conference held at Nagpur; World Hindi Day celebrated on this date
Official Languages Act passed by Parliament under Article 343(3)
Official Language Rules notified under Section 8(1) of OL Act 1963
Government's policy for use of Hindi in Central Government offices and PSUs strengthened
92nd Constitutional Amendment :added Bodo, Dogri, Maithili, Santali to 8th Schedule (total: 22)

cells: Hindi in Devanagari = Official Language of Union; English continued for 15 years; Parliament can extend
Rajbhasha Commission + Parliamentary Committee; constituted every 5 and 10 years
State legislature may adopt its own official language
English for Centre-State communications unless state and centre agree on Hindi
President may recognise language of substantial population of a state
SC, HC, Parliament :English till Parliament provides otherwise
Language bills need Presidential sanction; Rajbhasha Commission consulted
Right to petition in any language used in Union or State
Mother tongue instruction at primary level for linguistic minorities
Duty of Union to spread Hindi; draw from Sanskrit primarily; composite culture medium
Best performing Central Government offices in Hindi implementation; 3 regions × 3 categories
Citizens, organisations doing exceptional Hindi promotion; Rs.2 lakh to Rs.50,000
India's highest literary award; for lifetime contribution to Indian literature including Hindi
Annual literary award for each of 24 languages; Hindi category included; Rs.1 lakh
Padma Awards (Padma Vibhushan, Padma Bhushan, Padma Shri)
Conferred on distinguished Hindi scholars and writers for exceptional service to Hindi literature
Outstanding contribution to folk and classical arts; named after Tulsidas
Hindi/Urdu literature award; named after Munshi Premchand
Hindi has two genders: Pullinga (पुल्लिंग :masculine) and Striling (स्त्रीलिंग :feminine); no neuter; gender must be determined for correct usage
Ekvacan (एकवचन :singular) and Bahuvacan (बहुवचन :plural); rules: '-ा' → '-े' for most masculine; '-ी' → '-ियाँ' for most feminine

8 cases with vibhakti (postpositions): Kartaa (कर्ता :ने), Karma (कर्म :को), Karan (करण :से), Sampradaan (संप्रदान :के लिए), Apadaan (अपादान :से), Sambandh (संबंध :का/के/की), Adhikaran (अधिकरण :में/पर), Sambodhan (संबोधन :हे/ओ/अरे)
Hindi sentence order: Subject-Object-Verb (SOV); main verb at end; postpositions after noun (not prepositions)
First person (उत्तम पुरुष): मैं, हम; Second person (मध्यम पुरुष): तू/तुम/आप; Third person (अन्य पुरुष): वह/वे/यह/ये

items: Important Articles related to Rajbhasha are frequently asked in competitive exams.
Dates associated with Hindi/Rajbhasha milestones and major Hindi awards are critical high-yield topics.
Grammar quick references and topic checklists should be reviewed immediately prior to the exam.

8th Schedule 22 Languages: AaBo-DoGu-Hi-Ka-Ko-Ma-Ma-Ma-Ma-Ne-Od-Pu-Sa-San-Si-Ta-Te-Ur → Assamese, Bodo, Dogri, Gujarati, Hindi, Kannada, Konkani, Maithili, Malayalam, Manipuri, Marathi, Nepali, Odia, Punjabi, Sanskrit, Santali, Sindhi, Tamil, Telugu, Urdu (remember: 22 languages, 4 added in 2003 = Bodo, Dogri, Maithili, Santali)
Art. 343-351 covers Official Language :Remember: Hindi starts at 343; ends at 351 where duty to develop Hindi is given
Three Regions (A, B, C): A = All Hindi states (UMMRRHD :UP, MP, Bihar, Rajasthan, Haryana, Himachal, Uttarakhand, Delhi, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand); C = South India mostly; B = in between
Hindi Diwas vs World Hindi Day: Hindi Diwas = 14 September (Constituent Assembly adopted 1949); World Hindi Day = 10 January (First World Hindi Conference, Nagpur 1975)
Chhayavad Four Pillars: PPMS = Prasad, Pant, Mahadevi, Nirala (4 pillars of Chhayavad movement)
Bhakti Kaal Two Wings: Nirguna (Sant poets like Kabir, Nanak, Dadu) + Saguna (Vaishnava poets like Tulsidas, Surdas, Mira)
Samas: ATDKDB = Avyayibhav, Tatpurusha, Dvandva, Karmadharaya, Dvigu, Bahuvrihi (6 main types)
Sandhi Types: SVY = Swar (vowel), Vyanjan (consonant), Visarg (breath) :3 main types of Sandhi
OL Rules 1976 :Three Key Rules: Rule 4 = inter-office communication language; Rule 5 = state communication language; Rule 6 = public communication language

cells: Articles 343–351; Part XVII; 8th Schedule (22 languages); Constituent Assembly 14 Sept 1949; Hindi not National Language
Passed under Art.343(3); continued English indefinitely; authoritative English text for laws; Section 3 key; amended 1967
Rule 4 (inter-office); Rule 5 (state communication); Rule 6 (public); Region A/B/C classification; bilingual requirements
Town-level coordination; quarterly meetings; peer inspection; awards; half-yearly report to DoOL
Faithfulness; idiomacity; register appropriateness; CSTT terminology use; avoid literal translation
Swar, Vyanjan, Visarg :3 types; know Dirgha, Guna, Yan sandhi sub-types
6 types: Avyayibhav, Tatpurusha (with Karmadharaya, Dvigu sub-types), Dvandva, Bahuvrihi
Shabdalankar (Anupras, Yamak, Shlesh) vs Arthalankar (Upama, Rupak, Utpreksha, Atishyokti)
Tulsidas (Ramcharitmanas); Kabir (Bijak); Premchand (Godan); Jaishankar Prasad (Kamayani); Mahadevi Verma (Yama); Dinkar (Rashmirathi)
14 September (Hindi Diwas) vs 10 January (World Hindi Day); difference is critical
Training, translation, inspection, QPR, competitions, incentive scheme, technology, annual report
All key banking terms in Hindi; bilingual forms; ATM in Hindi; CBS Hindi module
